milestone.title: mp read ergonomics — projection, summary, note add fixes

intent.outcome: Agents read mp state with `mp <cmd> --fields / --summary` consistently across every read command (unknown path is a hard error everywhere, never silently ignored) and never reach for python3 -c for common projections. `mp note add` accepts `--body @file` / `@-` and errors clearly on invalid destinations. `mp milestone create --json @file` round-trips `design_decisions` (mirroring acceptance_criteria); `update` stays fragment-first and keeps rejecting the array.

problem.description: Verified audit of the current CLI: `--fields` is already honored by mp status, mp list milestones, mp reviews finding list, and mp reviews lifecycle (unknown path errors), but silently IGNORED by mp path and mp inbox — so the surface is inconsistent and an unknown path can pass silently. `--summary` exists on none of status / reviews finding list / reviews lifecycle. `mp note add` is undocumented in the master-planner skill, only accepts inline bodies (shell-backtick mangling on markdown), and has no @file/@- escape. `mp milestone create --json` silently drops a `design_decisions` array because CreateMilestoneInput has no such field (serde ignores unknown keys); `mp milestone update --json` correctly rejects it today with a hint to `mp milestone design-decision add`. All four frictions surfaced across the M93/M94/M95 sessions and the M97/M98/M99 creation pass.

in_scope: Close --fields gaps: mp path and mp inbox must honor --fields and error on unknown paths (parity with mp show milestone / status / list milestones / reviews commands)
Add --summary to: mp status (headline metrics, no path block), mp reviews finding list (open/fixed/total counts only), mp reviews lifecycle (bucket counts only)
--fields parity regression test: unknown path is a hard error across ALL read commands (status, path, inbox, list milestones, reviews finding list, reviews lifecycle, show milestone)
mp note add --body @<path> reads body from file; --body @- reads from stdin (avoids shell-backtick mangling of inline markdown)
mp note add --to <invalid> errors with the list of valid destinations

Add design_decisions field to CreateMilestoneInput so mp milestone create --json @file round-trips the field instead of silently dropping it (mirrors how acceptance_criteria is accepted at create time)
AGENT-READINESS.md and master-planner SKILL.md updated with the --fields parity, --summary modes, and --body @file/@- syntax
Integration tests in crates/mp/tests/read_ergonomics.rs and crates/mp/tests/note_add.rs
out_of_scope: Backward-compat shims for python3 -c patterns (callers can migrate)
Field projection on write commands (only reads need it)

design_decisions round-trip via mp milestone update --json — stays fragment-first (mp milestone design-decision add), consistent with acceptance_criteria being a guarded document array on update (M93 discipline)
Bulk read endpoints (covered by M94 bulk ops for writes)
JSON streaming / NDJSON mode (not needed at this size)

design_decisions.rationale: CreateMilestoneInput gains the design_decisions field so mp milestone create --json @file populates it (mirrors acceptance_criteria, which is also accepted at create time). The earlier DD text ('both accept the design_decisions array now') was aspirational and is corrected here: only create round-trips; update does not.

findings.description: resolve_body (note.rs:55-73) treats ANY --body value starting with '@' as a path/stdin sentinel, with no escape. A legitimate body that starts with '@' — '@username ping', '@channel fyi', a markdown '@decorator', an email-style handle — is silently reinterpreted as a file read and fails with 'could not read body file: username ping'. Reproducer: 'mp note add --title x --body "@username ping"' exits 1 with that error. There is no way to make a body whose first line starts with '@'. The spec (AC-07) says --body @file.txt, but didn't consider the collision with content. Conventional fix (jq --rawfile, git --output=, kubectl -f): add a separate --body-file <path> flag for the file/stdin path, and let --body always be literal inline text. Keeps AC-07/AC-08 working via the new flag and removes the ambiguity entirely. Backward-compat option: keep @file/@- on --body but add --body-file as the unambiguous path and document the @ escape (e.g. @@ for a literal leading @).
findings.author: zcode-review

findings.description: resolve_body uses std::path::Path::new(rest) which does NOT expand '~'. A natural '--body @~/notes.md' (quoted to prevent shell expansion, or in a script) fails with 'could not read body file: ~/notes.md' — confusing because the same path works unquoted on the shell. Reproducer: mp note add --title x --body '@~/note-test-marker' → exit 1. Rust std deliberately doesn't expand ~ (no HOME context at Path layer). Fix options: (a) document that @~/... is unsupported and the error message should hint 'tilde not expanded, use an absolute path'; (b) expand a leading '~/' manually via dirs::home_dir() or std::env::var("HOME"). Low severity because absolute paths and shell-expanded ~ both work; only the quoted-tilde case is affected.
findings.author: zcode-review
